turns.text: quick q. need to fit 2 practice quizzes + subnetting drills around my swing shift this week. i start at 2pm mon-fri and get out at 10:30. i use a practice-test app and a secondhand study guide with tabbed chapters. subnetting and port numbers keep tripping me up so put extra time there. can u make a weekly plan

Yep, here's a plan built around a 2 p.m. start, with study blocks ending before you leave for work.

**Mon-Fri mornings (before ~1 p.m.)**
- Mon: Practice quiz #1 in the app (about 45 min), then review every miss against the matching tab in your study guide.
- Tue: Subnetting drills, 45 min. Do CIDR notation and subnet masks by hand, no calculator.
- Wed: Port numbers, 30 min of flashcards, plus a 20 min chapter skim from your tabbed guide.
- Thu: Subnetting again, 45 min. Mix in problems that ask for the number of hosts per subnet.
- Fri: Practice quiz #2 (about 45 min), then 15 min logging which topics you missed.

**Weekend**
- Sat: One longer block (60-90 min) on whatever Friday's quiz showed was weakest, with extra time on subnetting and port numbers.
- Sun: Light review only, around 20 min.

**Tips**
- Stop everything about an hour before you head out so you're not rushing.
- Keep a running list of missed port numbers and reread it each morning.

Want me to generate some subnetting practice problems for Tuesday?
ty. also iris is out 8-5 weekdays so evenings and weekends are our time, dont want to eat into that. does this work

Yes, it does. Everything above sits in the mornings before your shift, so your evenings are untouched. The one weekend block is the only thing that overlaps with shared time.

To protect weekends further:
- Do the Saturday block early, say 9-10:30 a.m., so the rest of the day is free.
- If Sunday feels crowded, skip it and just glance at your missed-ports list for 10 min.
- If a weekday morning gets eaten, move that session to Saturday instead of squeezing it into the evening.

That gives you two full quizzes, three subnetting sessions and a port-number session while keeping your time with Iris free. Want a one-page version to stick on your desk?

- Mon: quiz #1 + review misses
- Tue: subnetting (45 min)
- Wed: port numbers flashcards + guide skim
- Thu: subnetting again
- Fri: quiz #2 + log weak spots
- Sat AM: one block on the weakest topic
- Sun: 10-20 min review, or skip
- All study done before you leave for your shift; evenings stay free
